purpose: Preserve retrieval history and verification limitations while the source registry records fixed editions and mathematical scope.

changes.current_note: Theorem 2.3.3 gives the one-dimensional finite-extension decomposition into exponential twists of regular differential modules, with descent; specialize to ℂ((z)). Roadmap §1.1 constructs the relative generic I23 factorization, and §4.1 constructs analytic Stokes data.

changes.previous_note: Chosen logarithmic extension is not in general tensor-compatible. General prescribed resonant lattices/flags, their families and determinant comparisons remain explicit owned extensions; do not infer them from a bare equivalence with local systems. II6.6 supplies the exact proof route for bounded complexes with differential-operator differentials: analytify the O-linear principal-parts presentation, then compare the E1 terms of the hypercohomology spectral sequence using proper GAGA.
changes.current_note: II5.4 constructs a chosen logarithmic extension, which is not in general tensor-compatible; roadmap §§2.5–2.6 construct the comparisons for prescribed resonant lattices, flags, families and determinants. II6.6 gives the bounded differential-operator-complex comparison by analytifying the O-linear principal-parts presentation and applying proper GAGA to the E1 terms of its hypercohomology spectral sequence.

changes.previous_note: Flat finitely presented central subgroup embedded functorially in inertia; the required cases are Gm and μr over ℂ. Connection-specific identification with the GIT coarse family is additional work.
changes.current_note: Rigidification by a flat finitely presented separated group scheme embedded functorially as a central subgroup of inertia; the cases used here are Gm and μr over ℂ. Roadmap §1.3 identifies the rigidification with the connection GIT coarse family.

changes.previous_note: Proper flat fp family with O_T≅f_(T,*)O_(X_T) for every T gives Picard algebraic space; lfp/quasiseparated; relative dimension≤1 gives smoothness. changes.current_note: For a proper flat finitely presented family with O_T≅f_(T,*)O_(X_T) for every T, the relative Picard functor is a locally finitely presented, quasiseparated algebraic space; relative dimension at most one gives smoothness. Nonreduced curves and test bases are included. Roadmap §§1.5 and 5.1 construct the component, dimension and additive Ga comparisons.
